metadata.data_source: KPMG Datacenter Intelligence Unit — Compiled from public filings, operator disclosures, and market research (2024-2026)
metadata.notes: Capacity figures represent commissioned IT load unless stated otherwise. Tenant lists are indicative based on publicly known anchor clients.

datacenters.name: Yotta NM1 — Hiranandani Fortune City
datacenters.cooling_type: Chilled Water with Hot/Cold Aisle Containment
datacenters.notable_facts: India's first hyperscale data center park. Houses over 7,200 racks across 5 buildings with an eventual buildout target of 200 MW.

datacenters.name: STT GDC Mumbai DC1 — Airoli
datacenters.notable_facts: Part of STT GDC's INR 5,000 crore MoU with Maharashtra for AI-ready datacenter expansion at Palava campus targeting 400 MW.

datacenters.name: Equinix MB1 — Chandivali
datacenters.cooling_type: Precision Air Cooling with Hot Aisle Containment
datacenters.notable_facts: Equinix's first IBX datacenter in India. Acquired additional 1.38 acres in Chandivali for INR 155 crore to expand Mumbai presence.

datacenters.name: Equinix CN1 — Chennai
datacenters.notable_facts: Equinix's first AI-ready datacenter in India, opened September 2025 with USD 69 million investment. Connected to three Mumbai IBX facilities.

datacenters.name: NTT Chennai 1 — Ambattur
datacenters.cooling_type: Chilled Water with Variable Frequency Drives
datacenters.notable_facts: NTT's Chennai campus supports the second-highest submarine cable density in India after Mumbai.

datacenters.name: CtrlS Hyderabad DC — Rajendranagar
datacenters.cooling_type: Precision Cooling with Free Air Economizer
datacenters.notable_facts: Asia's first Tier IV certified datacenter. CtrlS signed MoU with Telangana government for 400 MW expansion at Chandan Valley.

datacenters.name: NTT Bengaluru 4 — Whitefield
datacenters.cooling_type: Liquid Cooling + Chilled Water — AI/HPC Ready
datacenters.notable_facts: NTT's 4th Bengaluru campus spanning 8.5 acres with INR 2,400 crore investment. Phase 4A (22.4 MW) already operational.

datacenters.name: Nxtra by Airtel — Manesar
datacenters.notable_facts: Part of Nxtra's 14-datacenter India portfolio with 200 MW total capacity. Bharti Airtel investing $600 million in expansion.

datacenters.name: Equinix SG1 — One-North
datacenters.notable_facts: Most network-dense carrier-neutral datacenter in Southeast Asia. Home to one of three global GRX peering points. Part of Equinix's 5-facility Singapore campus.

datacenters.name: Digital Realty SIN10 — Loyang
datacenters.notable_facts: Multi-story 50 MW facility with 100% renewable energy coverage through direct retail energy agreements. Part of PlatformDIGITAL ecosystem.

datacenters.name: STT GDC Singapore 6 — Tai Seng
datacenters.notable_facts: Singapore's first NVIDIA DGX Ready certified datacenter (2025). Features liquid cooling for dense AI deployments and GPU-as-a-Service capabilities.

datacenters.name: AirTrunk SGP1 — Loyang
datacenters.notable_facts: AirTrunk secured SGD 2.3 billion green loan in 2025 for SGP2 expansion targeting 70+ MW AI-powered capacity.

datacenters.name: Keppel DC Singapore 4 — Gul Circle
datacenters.notable_facts: Part of Keppel DC REIT portfolio — one of Asia's few pure-play datacenter REITs listed on SGX.

datacenters.name: Digital Realty DUB10 — Profile Park
datacenters.cooling_type: Free Air Cooling — Temperate Climate Optimized
datacenters.notable_facts: Digital Realty is Ireland's largest operator. Dublin has the third-largest datacenter market in Europe at 738 MW, behind only London and Amsterdam.

datacenters.name: Equinix DB3 — Blanchardstown
datacenters.notable_facts: Located in Dublin's key interconnection zone. Ireland's data centers consume 21% of national electricity — Dublin has paused new builds until 2028.

datacenters.name: Echelon Data Centres DUB20 — Clondalkin
datacenters.notable_facts: Echelon is one of Ireland's largest upcoming capacity contributors. Uses zero mechanical cooling — industry-leading PUE of 1.20.

datacenters.name: EdgeConneX — Cork
datacenters.notable_facts: Cork diversifies Ireland's datacenter geography beyond Dublin. Benefits from proximity to Apple's European HQ and pharma manufacturing corridor.

datacenters.name: Equinix LD5 — Slough Campus
datacenters.cooling_type: Chilled Water with Free Cooling Economizer
datacenters.notable_facts: Part of Equinix's Slough campus (LD4/5/6/10) with 67 MW combined. Slough is the UK's second-largest datacenter hub after London proper. UK is Equinix's second-biggest market globally.

datacenters.name: VIRTUS London INCEPTION — Hayes
datacenters.cooling_type: Indirect Evaporative Cooling with Adiabatic Assist
datacenters.notable_facts: VIRTUS has overtaken Equinix as the UK's largest datacenter operator by total capacity. Parent STT GDC reports 78% renewable energy across portfolio.

datacenters.name: Digital Realty LON1 — Sovereign House, Docklands
datacenters.notable_facts: Digital Realty expanded to 14 UK facilities after USD 200 million Slough acquisition in July 2024. Equinix, Digital Realty, and NTT control over 44% of London's installed MW.

datacenters.name: Kao Data MAN1 — Manchester
datacenters.notable_facts: Manchester is the UK's fastest-growing datacenter market outside London. Kao Data specializes in high-performance computing and AI workloads.

datacenters.name: Vantage Data Centres — Newport
datacenters.notable_facts: Newport is emerging as a key UK datacenter hub outside the Greater London area, benefiting from lower land costs and Welsh Government incentives.

datacenters.name: Equinix DC2 — Ashburn

submarine_cables: Virginia Beach Cable Landing Station access

datacenters.notable_facts: Critical interconnection point in the datacenter capital of the world. Northern Virginia has 665+ datacenters and 4,000 MW of power — up to 70% of global internet traffic transits Loudoun County daily.

datacenters.name: QTS Ashburn — Mega Data Center
datacenters.notable_facts: One of the largest single-campus datacenters in Northern Virginia. Blackstone-owned QTS is driving aggressive expansion to serve AI demand.

datacenters.name: AWS US-East-1 — Haymarket Campus
datacenters.cooling_type: Custom Evaporative + Liquid Cooling for AI Racks
datacenters.notable_facts: The original AWS US-East-1 region — the world's most-used cloud availability zone. AWS is investing $9 billion in Virginia for 2026 expansion.

datacenters.name: CyrusOne Dallas — Carrollton Campus
datacenters.notable_facts: Dallas is a major hub with nearly 200 datacenters. Texas ranks second in the US with 413 facilities and 2.9 GW capacity (plus 3.1 GW planned).

datacenters.name: Microsoft Azure South Central — San Antonio
datacenters.notable_facts: Microsoft is investing $40 billion in Texas AI datacenter infrastructure through 2027. San Antonio campus serves as a critical US government cloud hub.

datacenters.name: Switch SUPERNAP — Austin
datacenters.cooling_type: Patented Hot/Cold Aisle with Free Cooling
datacenters.notable_facts: Switch operates with industry-leading PUE of 1.18. Austin is rapidly growing as a tech and AI datacenter hub alongside Dallas.

datacenters.name: Equinix SV5 — Silicon Valley
datacenters.cooling_type: Chilled Water with Precision Air Handling
datacenters.notable_facts: Equinix is building SV12x — a USD 600 million JV with PGIM Real Estate for 28+ MW xScale capacity in Silicon Valley.

datacenters.name: Google Cloud — The Dalles, Oregon
datacenters.cooling_type: Custom Evaporative Cooling — Columbia River Water
datacenters.notable_facts: One of Google's earliest and largest datacenter campuses. Achieves industry-leading PUE of 1.10 using Columbia River for evaporative cooling. Google's US active IT capacity is 508 MW.

datacenters.name: Digital Realty CHI1 — Chicago
datacenters.cooling_type: Chilled Water with Lake Michigan Water Access
datacenters.notable_facts: Chicago is a critical financial datacenter hub. Digital Realty signed agreements for 130+ MW of hyperscale capacity across Chicago, Dallas, Phoenix, and Virginia.

datacenters.name: QTS Atlanta — Suwanee Mega Campus
datacenters.notable_facts: Atlanta/Georgia has gained significant momentum in datacenter supply. QTS Suwanee is one of the largest single-campus facilities in the Southeast US.

datacenters.name: AWS US-East-2 — Columbus Campus
datacenters.cooling_type: Evaporative Cooling with Liquid Cooling for AI Racks
datacenters.notable_facts: Ohio ranks third in US datacenter capacity at 1.6 GW with 2.4 GW planned. AWS invested $50 billion for over 1 GW of AI and supercomputing capacity for the US government.

datacenters.name: Global Switch Singapore — Tai Seng
datacenters.notable_facts: Global Switch's Tai Seng facility is a key carrier hotel in Southeast Asia. Strategic cooperation with TIME dotCom strengthens routes toward Indochina via Malaysia.

datacenters.name: GreenScale — Ennis Data Centre Campus
datacenters.notable_facts: GreenScale is a major contributor to Ireland's upcoming capacity. Ennis campus leverages Atlantic maritime climate for zero-mechanical-cooling operations with industry-leading PUE.

datacenters.name: Equinix TY11 — Shinagawa
datacenters.notable_facts: Equinix operates 18 datacenters in Japan with over 1 GW collective capacity. Tokyo is the world's second-largest colocation market.

datacenters.name: AT TOKYO Chuo Center (CC1)
datacenters.notable_facts: AT TOKYO is Japan's largest domestic datacenter operator. CC1 is one of Tokyo's premier carrier hotels and interconnection hubs.

datacenters.name: AirTrunk OSK1 — Osaka West
datacenters.notable_facts: Osaka is Japan's second-largest datacenter market. AirTrunk's TOK1 campus is scaling toward 300 MW total.

datacenters.name: KDDI Telehouse Osaka Sakai
datacenters.notable_facts: Built on former Sharp LCD plant site. Features immersion-cooled containers achieving PUE as low as 1.05-1.07 in trials. KDDI targeting carbon neutrality by FY2026.

datacenters.name: MC Digital Realty NRT10 — Inzai
datacenters.cooling_type: Chilled Water with Free Cooling Economizer
datacenters.notable_facts: MC Digital Realty is a JV between Mitsubishi Corporation and Digital Realty Trust serving Japan's hyperscale demand corridor in Chiba Prefecture.

datacenters.name: Sakura Internet Ishikari DC
datacenters.notable_facts: Hokkaido's cold climate enables near-zero mechanical cooling with PUE of 1.11. Japan's government promotes northern datacenters for disaster recovery diversification.

datacenters.name: AirTrunk SYD1 — Western Sydney
datacenters.notable_facts: Australia's first and largest hyperscale datacenter. AirTrunk operates 1.2+ GW across 5 Australian campuses. Blackstone acquired majority stake for AUD 24 billion in 2024.

datacenters.name: NEXTDC M2 — Melbourne
datacenters.cooling_type: Chilled Water with Hot Aisle Containment
datacenters.notable_facts: NEXTDC is ASX-listed and Australia's largest domestic datacenter operator. M2 is Melbourne's highest-rated facility at Tier IV.

datacenters.name: Equinix SY4 — Sydney
datacenters.notable_facts: Equinix operates 18 facilities across 6 Australian cities with 730,000 sqft total capacity. Sydney and Melbourne house 80% of Australian datacenter capacity.

datacenters.name: CDC Canberra — Eastern Creek
datacenters.notable_facts: Australia's leading sovereign datacenter operator. CDC holds Protected-level IRAP certification for classified government workloads.

datacenters.name: NEXTDC P2 — Perth
datacenters.notable_facts: Perth serves Australia's mining and resources sector which requires low-latency edge compute for autonomous operations. Direct ASC submarine cable link to Singapore.

datacenters.name: Equinix FR5 — Frankfurt
datacenters.cooling_type: Chilled Water with Waste Heat Recovery
datacenters.notable_facts: Frankfurt is Europe's largest datacenter market and home to DE-CIX, the world's largest internet exchange by traffic. Germany has 529 datacenters — second in Europe.

datacenters.name: Digital Realty FRA15 — Frankfurt
datacenters.notable_facts: Part of Digital Realty's PlatformDIGITAL ecosystem in the FLAP-D corridor. Frankfurt hosts over 700 MW of datacenter capacity.

datacenters.name: NTT Berlin 1
datacenters.cooling_type: Free Cooling with Waste Heat Export
datacenters.notable_facts: NTT Berlin 1 exports waste heat to neighboring residential buildings — a model for German datacenter sustainability regulations.

datacenters.name: Equinix AM5 — Amsterdam Science Park
datacenters.notable_facts: Amsterdam is a FLAP-D market with 500+ MW capacity. AMS-IX peak traffic exceeds 12.7 Tbps across 878 connected networks. Amsterdam has a moratorium on new 70+ MW builds.

datacenters.name: Digital Realty AMS11 — Schiphol
datacenters.notable_facts: Schiphol-Rijk is Amsterdam's premier datacenter corridor. Netherlands has 298 datacenters and is Europe's fourth-largest market.

datacenters.name: Equinix PA8 — Paris
datacenters.notable_facts: Paris overtook Amsterdam as Europe's third-largest datacenter market in 2025. France has 322 datacenters nationally.

datacenters.name: Interxion MRS3 — Marseille
datacenters.notable_facts: Marseille is a critical subsea cable landing station connecting Europe to Africa, Middle East and Asia. Hosts 16+ submarine cables — second only to Singapore in EMEA.

datacenters.name: Data4 Paris-Saclay Campus
datacenters.cooling_type: Free Cooling with Ground-Source Heat Pumps
datacenters.notable_facts: Data4 is one of Europe's largest datacenter operators with Brookfield investing $20.7 billion in French AI infrastructure over 5 years starting 2025.

datacenters.name: KT Mokdong IDC — Seoul
datacenters.notable_facts: KT is South Korea's largest telecom and domestic datacenter operator. Seoul hosts 60% of Korea's datacenter capacity.

datacenters.name: Equinix SL1 — Seoul
datacenters.cooling_type: Precision Air with Hot Aisle Containment
datacenters.notable_facts: South Korea's datacenter market is growing rapidly driven by K-content streaming, gaming, and AI. Korea-Japan submarine cable consortium announced in 2025.

datacenters.name: Khazna Data Centers — DXB1
datacenters.notable_facts: Khazna is the largest datacenter operator in the Middle East. G42 partnership with Microsoft brings massive AI infrastructure investment to UAE.

datacenters.name: Moro Hub — Abu Dhabi
datacenters.notable_facts: Moro Hub is part of DEWA's smart city initiative. Abu Dhabi is positioning itself as a regional AI hub with sovereign AI compute infrastructure.

datacenters.name: STC Cloud Campus — Riyadh
datacenters.notable_facts: Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 is driving massive datacenter investment. Aramco, STC, and NEOM collectively planning over 1 GW of datacenter capacity.

datacenters.name: Bezeq Data Center — Tel Aviv
datacenters.notable_facts: Israel's datacenter market serves the 'Startup Nation' ecosystem. AWS and Google both launched local cloud regions in Israel in 2023.

datacenters.name: Equinix SP4 — São Paulo
datacenters.notable_facts: São Paulo is Latin America's largest datacenter market. Brazil benefits from abundant hydroelectric renewable energy powering 85%+ of the grid.

datacenters.name: Ascenty SP1 — Campinas
datacenters.notable_facts: Ascenty (Digital Realty/Brookfield JV) is Latin America's largest datacenter operator with 34+ facilities across Brazil, Chile, Mexico, and Colombia.

datacenters.name: Ascenty SCL1 — Santiago
datacenters.notable_facts: Chile has Latin America's cleanest energy grid (95%+ renewable). Google's Curie subsea cable connects Chile directly to Los Angeles.

datacenters.name: Equinix BG1 — Bogotá
datacenters.notable_facts: Bogotá's high altitude (2,640m) provides natural cooling advantages. Colombia is a strategic hub connecting Central and South American networks.

datacenters.name: Teraco JB1 — Johannesburg
datacenters.notable_facts: Teraco (acquired by Digital Realty) is Africa's largest carrier-neutral datacenter operator. JB1 hosts NAPAfrica — Africa's largest internet exchange point.

datacenters.name: Teraco CT1 — Cape Town
datacenters.notable_facts: Cape Town is Africa's second datacenter hub. Meta's 2Africa subsea cable (45,000 km, largest ever) lands here connecting Africa to Europe and Middle East.

datacenters.name: AirTrunk JHB1 — Johor Bahru
datacenters.notable_facts: AirTrunk announced $2.5 billion Malaysian datacenter investment. Johor is the overflow market for Singapore, offering lower costs with cross-border fiber links.

datacenters.name: AIMS Data Centre — Cyberjaya
datacenters.notable_facts: Cyberjaya is Malaysia's dedicated tech hub and MSC Malaysia zone. TIME dotCom's network provides connectivity to Singapore's ecosystem.

datacenters.name: DCI Indonesia — Jakarta
datacenters.notable_facts: Indonesia is Southeast Asia's largest internet market with 200M+ users. Jakarta's datacenter market is expanding rapidly to serve domestic cloud demand.

datacenters.name: NTT Jakarta 3
datacenters.notable_facts: NTT announced large-scale datacenter developments in Indonesia in 2025 with advanced cooling technologies.

datacenters.name: Equinix HK1 — Kwai Chung
datacenters.notable_facts: Hong Kong is Asia's premier financial interconnection hub with access to both China and global markets. Equinix operates 5 facilities here.

datacenters.name: SUNeVision MEGA Plus — Tseung Kwan O
datacenters.notable_facts: Tseung Kwan O is Hong Kong's submarine cable landing station district and the city's largest datacenter corridor. MEGA Plus is one of Asia's most connected facilities.

datacenters.name: Equinix SK1 — Stockholm
datacenters.notable_facts: Sweden runs on 98% fossil-free electricity. Stockholm datacenters export waste heat to the city's district heating system serving 200,000 homes.

datacenters.name: Green Mountain DC1-Stavanger
datacenters.notable_facts: Built inside a former NATO ammunition storage facility in a mountain. Uses fjord water at 8°C for free cooling achieving PUE of 1.10. Norway has 100% hydroelectric power.

datacenters.name: Equinix HE7 — Helsinki
datacenters.notable_facts: Helsinki offers 10 months of free cooling annually and 100% carbon-free electricity. Finland is a strategic gateway between EU and Asian networks via Arctic routes.

datacenters.name: Interxion CPH2 — Copenhagen
datacenters.cooling_type: Free Cooling with District Heat Export
datacenters.notable_facts: Copenhagen aims to be carbon-neutral by 2025. Danish datacenters export heat to city systems. Apple abandoned a 1 billion euro datacenter in Denmark in 2024.

datacenters.name: Equinix TR2 — Toronto
datacenters.notable_facts: Toronto is Canada's largest datacenter market. Canadian data sovereignty requirements drive local infrastructure investment. Canada has 337 datacenters nationally.

datacenters.name: QScale Q01 — Lévis
datacenters.notable_facts: Quebec offers North America's cheapest electricity via hydropower (100% renewable). QScale is purpose-built for AI/HPC workloads using Canada's cold climate for free cooling.

datacenters.name: Cologix VAN3 — Vancouver
datacenters.notable_facts: Vancouver is a gateway between North American and Asian networks. BC's hydroelectric grid provides near-100% renewable power at competitive rates.

datacenters.name: Equinix QR1 — Querétaro
datacenters.notable_facts: Querétaro is Mexico's primary datacenter hub, benefiting from seismic stability and high altitude for natural cooling. Mexico is Latin America's second-largest market.

datacenters.name: Equinix ZH4 — Zürich
datacenters.notable_facts: Switzerland's strict data privacy laws (nFADP) make it a premium location for sensitive data. Zürich uses Lake Zürich water for free cooling.

datacenters.name: Equinix MD2 — Madrid
datacenters.notable_facts: Madrid is Southern Europe's fastest-growing datacenter market. EllaLink cable connects Spain to Brazil directly, making Madrid a Europe-LatAm bridge.

datacenters.name: Equinix ML5 — Milan
datacenters.notable_facts: Milan is part of the FLAP-D+M corridor. Italy added Milan to Europe's top datacenter markets with 350+ MW capacity.

datacenters.name: Africa Data Centres — Nairobi
datacenters.notable_facts: Kenya is East Africa's datacenter hub. Nairobi's high altitude (1,795m) provides natural cooling. Africa Data Centres is building 10+ facilities across the continent.

datacenters.name: Rack Centre — Lagos
datacenters.notable_facts: Equinix acquired Rack Centre in 2024 marking its entry into Africa. Lagos serves West Africa's largest economy (220M+ population). Grid reliability remains a challenge with diesel backup.

datacenters.name: CDC Auckland — Albany
datacenters.notable_facts: CDC's first New Zealand facility. NZ offers 85%+ renewable electricity (hydro + geothermal). Southern Cross NEXT cable provides 72 Tbps connectivity to Sydney and the US.

datacenters.name: Chief Telecom — Taipei
datacenters.notable_facts: Taiwan is critical for the global semiconductor supply chain (TSMC). Taipei datacenters serve the chip design and AI model inference ecosystem.

datacenters.name: TRUE IDC — Bangkok
datacenters.notable_facts: AWS launched a Thailand region in January 2025 with $5 billion investment. Bangkok is emerging as a key Southeast Asian datacenter market alongside Singapore and Jakarta.

datacenters.name: Viettel IDC — Ho Chi Minh City
datacenters.notable_facts: Vietnam is one of Southeast Asia's fastest-growing digital economies with 78M+ internet users. AWS and Google both expanding cloud presence in Vietnam.

datacenters.name: CyrusOne Chandler — Phoenix
datacenters.notable_facts: Phoenix is the US's second-largest datacenter hub with 100+ facilities and 1,380 MW capacity. Arizona's abundant solar energy and dry climate enable efficient evaporative cooling.

datacenters.name: Switch Las Vegas — The Citadel
datacenters.notable_facts: Switch's SUPERNAP campus is one of the world's largest. Achieved industry-first Tier IV Gold certification. Operates at PUE 1.18 with 100% renewable energy in the desert.

datacenters.name: Microsoft Quincy — Columbia River
datacenters.notable_facts: Quincy benefits from Grant County PUD's hydroelectric rates — among the cheapest power in the US. Microsoft uses Columbia River basin water for evaporative cooling.

datacenters.name: Meta — Altoona
datacenters.notable_facts: Iowa's wind energy enables 100% renewable operations. Meta's Altoona campus achieves industry-best PUE of 1.08. One of the largest AI training infrastructure sites globally.

datacenters.name: CtrlS Kolkata DC1
datacenters.cooling_type: Chilled Water with Hot Aisle Containment
datacenters.notable_facts: Kolkata is the datacenter gateway to Eastern and Northeastern India. Expected to lead Indian markets with 48% CAGR. CtrlS invested USD 482 million in Chennai campus.

datacenters.name: AdaniConneX — Noida
datacenters.cooling_type: Hybrid Cooling — Free Air + Chilled Water
datacenters.notable_facts: AdaniConneX (Adani-EdgeConneX 50:50 JV) partnered with Google for India's largest AI datacenter campus. Platform targets 1 GW across India.

datacenters.name: Digital Realty SIN12 — Tuas
datacenters.cooling_type: Seawater Cooling — LNG Waste Heat Sink
datacenters.notable_facts: Tuas leverages LNG-regasification plants as waste heat sinks to achieve sub-1.2 PUE. Part of Singapore's Green Data Centre Roadmap for CFA-approved sustainable builds.

datacenters.name: Colt Tokyo Shiohama
datacenters.notable_facts: Colt operates across 9 Japanese cities. Tokyo has 74 existing and 26 upcoming datacenters as of 2025.

datacenters.name: Raya Data Center — Cairo
datacenters.notable_facts: Egypt is Africa's largest submarine cable landing nation with 15+ cables. The 2Africa cable (45,000 km) connects Egypt to 33 countries.

datacenters.name: Equinix LS1 — Lisbon
datacenters.notable_facts: Lisbon is a critical Atlantic subsea cable hub. EllaLink connects Europe to Brazil directly. Equiano cable connects to West Africa. Portugal runs 80%+ on renewables.

datacenters.name: PLDT ePLDT VITRO Makati
datacenters.notable_facts: Philippines is Southeast Asia's BPO capital driving colocation demand. Manila has 20+ operational datacenters serving 110M+ population.

datacenters.name: Verne Global — Keflavik Campus
datacenters.cooling_type: 100% Free Air — Arctic Climate + Geothermal Power
datacenters.notable_facts: World's lowest PUE at 1.03 — entirely free-air cooled in Arctic climate. 100% geothermal and hydroelectric power at Europe's cheapest electricity rates. Built on a former NATO air base. Carbon-neutral since 2020.

datacenters.name: AWS Asia Pacific (Mumbai) Region — ap-south-1
datacenters.notable_facts: AWS's first India region launched in 2016 with 3 AZs. AWS announced $8.3 billion expansion in Mumbai (MoU signed at Davos Jan 2025). Part of $12.7 billion total India investment by 2030. Also planning $430 million new facility in Navi Mumbai (49-acre Taloja site).

datacenters.name: AWS Asia Pacific (Hyderabad) Region — ap-south-2
datacenters.notable_facts: AWS's second India region (30th globally) launched Nov 2022. $7 billion Hyderabad expansion supports AI/ML workloads. AWS partnering with Tata Communications for high-capacity Mumbai-Hyderabad-Chennai backbone for GenAI and HPC.

datacenters.name: Microsoft Azure Central India — Pune
datacenters.notable_facts: Azure's first India region (Central India) launched 2015 — Microsoft was the first major US cloud provider in India. Only Indian Azure region with Availability Zones (added Dec 2021). 99.99% uptime SLA. Part of Microsoft's $17.5 billion India investment (2026-2029).

datacenters.name: Microsoft Azure South India — Chennai
datacenters.notable_facts: Azure South India launched alongside Pune and Mumbai in 2015. Chennai is India's second-largest datacenter market at 21% of national capacity. Submarine cable connectivity to Singapore and Southeast Asia.

datacenters.name: Microsoft Azure India South Central — Hyderabad
datacenters.cooling_type: Liquid Cooling + Chilled Water — AI-Ready Hyperscale
datacenters.notable_facts: Microsoft's largest hyperscale region in India — 'roughly equivalent in size to two Eden Gardens stadiums combined.' Go-live mid-2026 with 3 AZs. Part of $17.5 billion India investment (largest in Asia). Microsoft acquired 115+ acres across Mekaguda, Shadnagar, and Chandenvelly.

datacenters.name: Google Cloud Mumbai Region — asia-south1
datacenters.notable_facts: Google's first India cloud region launched 2017 across 3 Mumbai datacenters. Blue-Raman subsea cable India segment went live Q4 2025 with Mumbai landing. Also building first self-developed facility in Navi Mumbai. Part of Google's $75 billion global capex.

datacenters.name: Google Cloud Delhi Region — asia-south2
datacenters.cooling_type: Custom Google Cooling — Dry Climate Benefit
datacenters.notable_facts: Google's second India region launched 2021 serving northern India. Delhi NCR's dry winter climate enables free cooling for several months. Supports India's growing government cloud adoption.

datacenters.name: Google-AdaniConneX AI Hub — Visakhapatnam
datacenters.owner_group: Alphabet Inc. / Adani Group / Bharti Airtel
datacenters.cooling_type: Liquid Cooling + Seawater Cooling — Coastal AI Infrastructure
datacenters.notable_facts: Google's largest investment outside the US at $15 billion (2026-2030). India's first gigawatt-scale datacenter. Three linked campuses across 480 acres in Adivivaram, Tarluvada, and Rambilli-Achyutapuram. Includes subsea cable landing station via Airtel. Groundbreaking April 28, 2026.

datacenters.name: Oracle Cloud Mumbai Region
datacenters.notable_facts: Oracle Cloud's first India region. OCI serves Indian government, banking, and enterprise workloads with data residency guarantees. Oracle is one of 8 major hyperscalers investing in India's datacenter ecosystem.

datacenters.name: Oracle Cloud Hyderabad Region
datacenters.notable_facts: Oracle's second India region for disaster recovery and multi-region architectures. Hyderabad has become India's second-largest cloud hub after Mumbai with AWS, Microsoft, Oracle, and Google all operating regions.

datacenters.name: Meta-Reliance Jio Data Hub — Mumbai
datacenters.owner_group: Meta Platforms Inc. / Reliance Industries Ltd.
datacenters.notable_facts: Meta-Reliance JV with Reliance holding 70% and Meta 30% — approximately ₹855 crore investment. Supports WhatsApp's 500M+ Indian users and Instagram's largest market outside US. Meta's 2Africa subsea cable lands in Mumbai.

datacenters.name: Reliance Jamnagar Gigawatt DC — Gujarat
datacenters.cooling_type: Liquid Cooling — AI/HPC Optimized + Renewable Powered
datacenters.notable_facts: Announced Jan 2025 — planned as one of the world's largest datacenters at 1 GW (expandable to 3 GW). Powered entirely by Reliance's 6 GW solar project. Secured NVIDIA Blackwell AI processors for India-specific LLMs. Located adjacent to the world's largest oil refinery complex.

datacenters.name: AWS Bengaluru — Local Zone
datacenters.notable_facts: AWS Local Zone in Bengaluru brings single-digit millisecond latency to India's tech capital. Bengaluru hosts 40% of India's tech workforce. AWS also has Local Zones in Delhi and Kolkata.

datacenters.name: Sify Ambattur AI-Hub — Chennai
datacenters.notable_facts: Sify is one of India's largest domestic datacenter operators (est. 1998). Chennai accounts for 21% of India's total datacenter capacity — second only to Mumbai. Sify's AI-Hub designed for GPU-dense racks up to 50kW per rack.
